options.label: Assigning an `XmlUrlResolver` makes `LoadXml` resolve external entities, so a declared SYSTEM entity reads local files or hits internal URLs during parsing
`decimal.Parse(total)` throws on non-numeric input, letting an attacker crash the importer
options.whyWrong: A parse exception is a robustness bug, not the disclosure/SSRF primitive the resolver creates.

options.label: The XPath in `SelectSingleNode` is built from input and can be injected
options.whyWrong: The XPath strings here are constant; nothing user-controlled is concatenated into them.

options.label: Disable the resolver so external entities are not fetched
Validate the XML against a schema after loading
options.whyWrong: Entity expansion happens during LoadXml, before validation runs, so external entities are already resolved and any SSRF/file read has occurred.

options.label: HTML-encode the parsed values before use
options.whyWrong: Output encoding addresses a different problem (XSS). It does nothing about entities resolved during parsing.

options.label: Wrap parsing in a size limit
options.whyWrong: A size cap mitigates one DoS variant (billion laughs) but still allows a small document with an external entity to read local files or make server-side requests.

training.exploit: Upload an invoice beginning with `<!DOCTYPE invoice [<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]>` and put `&x;` inside `<customer>`. During `LoadXml`, the parser reads the file and the customer value becomes its contents — which the app then stores or echoes. Swap in `SYSTEM "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/"` to pivot into server-side request forgery against internal services.

hints.line: One line flips the parser from safe to fetch-anything.
hints.bugClass: It's about what the XML parser will go and load.
hints.why: What does a resolver let a `<!ENTITY ... SYSTEM ...>` do?

writeup.summary: Setting `XmlResolver = new XmlUrlResolver()` tells the parser to resolve external entities and DTDs. A document declaring `<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">` and referencing `&x;` inside `<customer>` makes the parser read that file and place its contents in the parsed value; a `http://` system id turns it into server-side request forgery against internal hosts. On modern .NET the default resolver is already null, but explicitly assigning one re-enables the danger. The fix sets `XmlResolver = null`, so external references are never fetched. Schema validation and output encoding address other stages and don't stop entity resolution during `LoadXml`.
